standard_prerequisites.name: A quasi-coherent module as a filtered colimit of coherent modules, and cohomology of quasi-compact quasi-separated spaces commuting with such colimits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, labels lemma-directed-colimit-coherent (invoked at proof line 3262) and lemma-colimits (invoked at proof line 3266)
standard_prerequisites.use: They replace $j_*\mathcal{F}$ by the filtered colimit of coherent $\mathcal{F}_i$ and compute $H^1(X, j_*\mathcal{F})$ as the colimit of the $H^1(X, \mathcal{F}_i)$.

standard_prerequisites.name: Closed points of a decent Noetherian space, the schematic locus, and Noetherian sobriety
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Decent Spaces, label decent-spaces-lemma-decent-space-closed-point (invoked at proof line 3300), Properties of Spaces, label spaces-properties-lemma-subscheme (invoked at proof line 3320) and spaces-properties-lemma-Noetherian-sober (invoked at proof line 3328)
standard_prerequisites.use: They let every closed point be cut out by a closed immersion from a field, show that the closed points lie in the schematic locus once the $U$ are affine, and conclude that an open subset containing all closed points is everything.

standard_prerequisites.name: The scheme case of the criterion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology of Schemes, label coherent-lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-invertible (invoked at proof line 3331)
standard_prerequisites.use: Once $X$ is known to be a scheme, it converts the assumed vanishing into ampleness of $\mathcal{L}$.

core_obligations: Claim that for a global section $s \in H^0(X, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d})$ the open subspace $U$ over which $s$ generates $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}$ is affine, by showing $H^1(U, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{F}$ and invoking the affineness criterion (proof lines 3239-3248).

Use that $j : U \to X$ is affine, rewrite $H^1(U, \mathcal{F}) = H^1(X, j_*\mathcal{F})$, write $j_*\mathcal{F}$ as a filtered colimit of coherent $\mathcal{F}_i$, and reduce to showing that $H^1(X, \mathcal{F}_i) \to H^1(U, j^*\mathcal{F}_i)$ is zero (proof lines 3249-3267).

For fixed $i$, apply the hypothesis to the twisted direct sum to get $a \geq 0$ with $H^1(X, \mathcal{F}_i \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes ad}) = 0$; since $s^a$ is an isomorphism over $U$, the commutative diagram comparing the two restriction maps forces $H^1(X, \mathcal{F}_i) \to H^1(U, j^*\mathcal{F}_i)$ to be zero, proving the claim (proof lines 3268-3296).

For a closed point $x$, represent it by a closed immersion from the spectrum of a field, let $\mathcal{I}$ be the kernel of $\mathcal{O}_X \to i_*\mathcal{O}_{\Spec(k)}$, and choose $d$ with $H^1(X, \mathcal{I} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}) = 0$; the long exact sequence then makes $H^0(X, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}) \to k$ surjective, so some section has $x \in U$ and $x$ lies in the schematic locus (proof lines 3298-3321).

Conclude that $X$ is a scheme, since an open subset of the Noetherian space $|X|$ containing all closed points is everything, and finally obtain ampleness of $\mathcal{L}$ from the scheme case of the criterion (proof lines 3323-3332).
proof_roadmap: The claim that the nonvanishing open of a section is affine (proof lines 3239-3296).
Reduction to coherent modules through an affine inclusion and filtered colimits (proof lines 3249-3267).
Closed points lie in the schematic locus (proof lines 3298-3321).
$X$ is a scheme, and $\mathcal{L}$ is ample (proof lines 3323-3332).
difficulty_reason: The lemma extracts strong consequences from a cohomological hypothesis on a Noetherian algebraic space: vanishing of $H^1$ of all sufficiently high twists of coherent modules forces the space to be a scheme, with the invertible sheaf ample (statement lines 3228-3236). The proof shows that the open set where a section generates a fixed power of the sheaf is affine, using the affineness criterion, an affine inclusion, a filtered colimit presentation, and a twisting argument with the power of the section; it then uses closed points cut out by a field to reach the schematic locus and the Noetherian sobriety of the underlying space to conclude. The affineness claim is the substance, so the claim is H2.
